divisions.question: That the words proposed to be omitted ( **Mr Dutton’s** amendment) stand part of the question.
That items 1, 2 and 6 of schedule 1 and items 1, 2 and 6 of schedule 2 stand as printed.

speeches.speaker: Anne McEwen
speeches.brief: The Senate Standing Committee on Economics report on the Trade Practices Legislation Amendment Bill 2008, including proceedings and documents, was presented and ordered to be printed.

speeches.speaker: Kim Carr
speeches.brief: The Trade Practices Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 was moved to strengthen competition and fair trading laws, including amendments to clarify misuse of market power, remove recoupment as a necessary element for predatory pricing, require a small business expert on the ACCC, and extend unconscionable conduct protections by removing price thresholds.

speeches.speaker: George Brandis
speeches.brief: The opposition argued to retain the Birdsville amendment's market share test for predatory pricing, opposing its replacement with a market power test and the transfer of section 46 cases to the Federal Magistrates Court. The government and supporting speakers argued the bill strengthens the Trade Practices Act by clarifying market power, removing the recoupment requirement, and adding a small business deputy chair to the ACCC.

speeches.speaker: Nick Xenophon
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Trade Practices Act needs stronger misuse of market power provisions, citing the Boral case as an example where predatory pricing went unchecked. They supported the government's bill but raised concerns that proposed amendments to section 46 may not go far enough, and opposed scrapping the "Birdsville amendment" which uses market share as a test for predatory pricing.

speeches.speaker: George Brandis
speeches.brief: The opposition opposed government amendments to the Trade Practices Act that would introduce recoupment as a requirement in predatory pricing cases and give the Federal Magistrates Court jurisdiction over section 46 cases, arguing these changes would harm small businesses and not reduce costs. The government defended the amendments as clarifying the law and improving access to justice.

speeches.speaker: Nick Sherry
speeches.brief: Senator Xenophon's amendment to the Trade Practices Legislation Amendment Bill 2008 was agreed to without a division, and the bill as amended was passed.

The House of Representatives agreed to Senate amendments (1), (3), (4), (6) and (7) to the Trade Practices Legislation Amendment Bill 2008, disagreed to amendments (2) and (5), made six further amendments, and requested Senate reconsideration; the Senate ordered the message be considered in Committee of the Whole immediately.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The committee moved to accept the House of Representatives’ amendments and drop its own, and the motion was agreed to.
